messages:
Anya: Quick review request — I'm iterating on the sidebar regrouping and breadcrumb rules. Main question: when a user deep-links into a nested route (e.g. /projects/123/models/xyz/metrics) should we auto-expand the parent groups, or show a condensed header + an explicit 'show in nav' affordance? Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/console-nav-proto

Ryan: I think auto-expand is friendlier for discoverability, but scared of long lists pushing content down on small screens. Maybe expand only the path to the active item and collapse unrelated groups.

Sophie: Accessibility nit — if we auto-expand, keyboard focus needs to land on the active item, not the group header. Also aria-expanded must update and we should announce "Section X expanded, 5 items" for screen readers.

Matt: +1 to Sophie. Also consider a compact collapsed state that still shows the active item label inline (like a pill) so you don't lose context. Example: [Models ▸ xyz]. That helps deep-linked pages keep orientation. :thumbsup:

Danielle: For deep links that land on a modal/detail view, do we modify the URL to include the sidebar path? If not, breadcrumbs become the single source of truth and must be clickable. We should ensure breadcrumbs use pushState so navigation is reversible.

Anya: Good point. Current plan: URL reflects canonical resource (/projects/:p/models/:m), modals are secondary (query param ?preview=true). Breadcrumbs map to canonical path.

Ryan: Routing edgecase: what about pinned routes? If team pins a model under a custom group, deep-links must still resolve to the pin location. That implies we need a route->nav mapping service when rendering the console.

Sophie: Implementation details: keyboard nav order = nav toggle -> group headers -> items. If we auto-expand, ensure focus trap isn't broken. Use roving tabindex pattern. Also announce when deep-link auto-expands: "Navigated to Model xyz, navigation expanded".

Matt: UX copy tweak: breadcrumb crumbs are currently nouns only. For long names truncate with ellipses but show full name on hover and in breadcrumb tooltip. For screen readers, expose full name via aria-label.

Design-bot: Prototype published: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/console-nav-proto — Version: sidebar-reorg-v3. Commit: 9f8a7c.

Danielle: Small routing snippet idea — propose canonical paths like: 
```
/apps/:appId/projects/:projectId/models/:modelId
/apps/:appId/models/:modelId?group=custom-pin
```
and hash anchors only for in-page sections (#metrics). This keeps deep-links crisp and avoids mixing hash routing for canonical nav.

Anya: Thanks. Quick poll: prefer auto-expand path to active item (A), or leave collapsed + show pill with active label (B)? Reply with A or B.

Matt: A

Sophie: A (with the aria announcements)

Ryan: B if we expect >7 groups frequently on mobile, otherwise A.

Danielle: B for mobile, A for desktop — can we make it responsive? Expand on wide screens, pill on narrow.

Anya: Cool — I'll push a responsive variant: auto-expand on >= 1024px, pill + 'show in nav' affordance under 1024px. I'll add the ARIA announcement and keyboard focus changes to the spec. Leaving tasks: update router mapping doc, add accessibility acceptance criteria, and prototype mobile pill state. Planning to ship canary next week.

Ryan: Sounds good. If anyone has quick dev constraints call them out now.

Matt: Dev note — we need to be careful with CSS transitions during auto-expand to avoid layout shift that affects perceived performance. Consider transform-based animations for content area instead of height transitions on nav.

Sophie: I'll draft the a11y checklist and post it here before EOD.

Anya: Thanks team! :heart:
